statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains low during the weekend closure; hawkish rate repricing and unresolved Hormuz restrictions keep reopening-gap Stress high.
recommendation: Published posture: low Tail with high Stress; no live NQ price path is available to establish persistent mean-reversion failure.
headline: Weekend closure keeps Tail low while rates and Hormuz risks sustain Stress
body: NQ is closed for the weekend. Friday's Nasdaq fell 0.52% after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reinforced the inflation fight. Saturday reporting shows Iran still maintaining Hormuz restrictions and reduced shipping traffic. Shared Finviz context is older than 90 minutes and was excluded.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 published hourly assessments cover Friday's high-stress session and the weekend closure. Tail briefly reached blocking territory during Friday's downside extensions, then returned to the low band once live price-path risk ended.
outlookSummary: All 24 forecast hours remain before the Sunday evening U.S. NQ reopening. Tail stays low because no live one-way path can form; Stress remains high initially and can ease gradually if weekend rate and Hormuz headlines remain incremental.

forecast.analysis: Weekend closure persists. If no material new shock emerges, reopening-gap Stress stays high while Tail remains low without observable trend persistence.
Friday's tape is aging. Absent a fresh geopolitical or policy discontinuity, the closed market cannot confirm failed mean reversion or repeated extension.
No futures tape is available. Any new headline would first affect gap uncertainty; higher Tail would still require post-reopen one-way structure.
Closed markets prevent pullback-depth or session-extreme tests. Tail remains low unless a material weekend discontinuity alters reopening conditions.
As Saturday advances, stale price evidence reduces directional conviction. If headlines remain incremental, Stress can ease slightly while Tail stays low.
No synchronous NQ, yield, volatility or breadth signal can form while futures are closed. Reopening-gap uncertainty remains the main risk channel.
Without price discovery, persistent directional efficiency cannot be observed. A fresh energy or geopolitical shock would raise Stress before Tail.
The horizon remains pre-reopen. If weekend news stays contained, the weight of Friday's hawkish repricing can gradually decay without changing Tail state.
No U.S. cash or futures transition occurs in this hour. Cross-asset alignment must be reassessed after reopening rather than assumed in advance.
Weekend closure continues. Semiconductor and megacap Friday moves remain historical context only; they do not establish a future one-way NQ path.
Headline risk remains asymmetric because Hormuz restrictions are unresolved. Any escalation would be a reopening checkpoint, not evidence of trend persistence.
Late Saturday conditions remain tape-free. If diplomatic news is incremental, Stress can drift lower as no new market confirmation arrives.
No live retracement test is possible. Tail remains in the low band while confidence edges lower as Friday market evidence becomes progressively older.
Pre-reopen gap risk remains the key conditional channel. A material oil or rates shock could raise Stress, but Tail still requires observed post-open persistence.
With no futures trading, directional structure is unobservable. Stable headlines would allow high Stress to moderate without changing the low-Tail assessment.
The market remains closed. Any weekend policy or geopolitical surprise would alter the reopening distribution first, with Tail dependent on subsequent price behavior.
No price-path evidence is scheduled in this hour. The assessment therefore emphasizes gap uncertainty and avoids treating hypothetical alignment as observed.
Sunday approaches but NQ is still closed in this slot. Risk remains conditional on whether weekend headlines materially change the reopening setup.
The absence of live tape keeps Tail low. If no discontinuity emerges, Stress can continue easing as the reopening checkpoint draws closer.
No current-session NQ structure can form before the Sunday reopen. Future alignment across yields, volatility and technology leadership remains unobserved.
Reopening is still outside this forecast slot. A new shock could widen the expected gap, but persistent mean-reversion failure cannot yet be demonstrated.
Weekend evidence remains headline-driven rather than tape-driven. Tail stays low conditionally, while Stress reflects unresolved rates and Hormuz uncertainty.
The final forecast hour is still before NQ reopening. The next decisive Tail information will come from the actual opening gap, pullback quality and cross-asset confirmation.
